SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK FP-08: FHIRPath — §5.5.7 Quantity Conversion, §5.5.8 String Conversion, §5.5.9 Time Conversion. Test these items: toQuantity([unit]), convertsToQuantity([unit]), toString(), convertsToString(), toTime(), convertsToTime(). For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath N1 §5.5.7 toQuantity([unit : String]) / convertsToQuantity([unit : String]); §5 function argument rules
issues.evidence: Native C++ accepts invalid Quantity conversion argument forms. Repro from .temp/qa/fp08_skeptic_probe_before.json: 1.toQuantity('1','g') returned ["1 '1'"], fhirpath_quantity="1 '1'", fhirpath_is_valid=true; 1.convertsToQuantity('1','g') returned true; 1.toQuantity(1), 1.convertsToQuantity(1), and multi-item unit args ('1'|'g') also returned successful native results. Forced Python fallback correctly returned empty/NULL with fhirpath_is_valid=false for these argument errors.
issues.root_cause: Native evalFunction allowed toQuantity()/convertsToQuantity() with any nonzero argument count and converted the first unit argument through toString() without checking singleton String shape.
issues.resolution: Added native exact 0/1 arity checks and singleton String validation for optional Quantity unit arguments before conversion.
issues.verified_in: FP-08 probe after fix: 33 cases, 0 failures; pytest test_conversion_parity.py: 17 passed; native sqllogictest: 412 assertions; full conformance: 2822/2822

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath N1 §5.5.8 toString()/convertsToString(); §5.5.9 toTime()/convertsToTime(); §5 function argument rules
issues.evidence: FP-08 zero-argument converters accept argument-bearing/global forms. Repro: native s.toString(1) returned ['abc'] with fhirpath_is_valid=true; native time_min.toTime(1) returned ['14:30'] with fhirpath_is_valid=true; s.convertsToString(1) returned true in both native and fallback; convertsToString(s) and convertsToTime(time_min) returned true in forced fallback instead of invalid expression results.
issues.root_cause: Native evalFunction did not reject arguments to toString(), toTime(), convertsToString(), or convertsToTime(); Python fallback registry still permitted one-argument convertsToString()/convertsToTime() forms.
issues.resolution: Added native zero-argument arity checks and changed fallback registry metadata so toString(), toTime(), convertsToString(), and convertsToTime() accept only zero arguments.
issues.verified_in: FP-08 probe after fix: 33 cases, 0 failures; pytest test_conversion_parity.py: 17 passed; native sqllogictest: 412 assertions; full conformance: 2822/2822

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath N1 §5.5 conversion singleton rule and §5.5.8 toString() / §5.5.7 convertsToQuantity()
issues.evidence: Forced Python fallback treats some constant multi-item FP-08 conversions as valid empty results instead of singleton errors. Repro: fallback (1|2).toString() returned empty/NULL with fhirpath_is_valid=true while native returned fhirpath_is_valid=false; fallback (1|2).convertsToQuantity() also returned empty/NULL with fhirpath_is_valid=true.
issues.root_cause: Forced Python fallback toString() and converts_to_quantity() returned empty for multi-item input instead of raising singleton conversion errors, so fhirpath_is_valid() treated constant multi-item conversion expressions as valid.
issues.resolution: Changed fallback toString() and converts_to_quantity() helpers to raise FHIRPathError on multi-item input while preserving empty-input propagation.
issues.verified_in: FP-08 probe after fix: 33 cases, 0 failures; pytest test_conversion_parity.py: 17 passed; native sqllogictest: 412 assertions; full conformance: 2822/2822
